lead.hed: Misawa added an F-35 engine trainer so maintainers can drill without a live jet
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted overnight from Misawa Air Base: the 35th Fighter Wing added an F-35A Lightning II engine-run simulator so maintainers can train on aircraft systems without using a live jet. Instructors can run engine-fire and hydraulic-failure scenarios in a closed room. Staff Sgt. Joshua Owens said the trainer saves about $12,000 in fuel per class, or about $144,000 a year, and puts the aircraft back on the line. Official classes for maintainers begin in November. Official still from the trainer room, Sept. 24.
lead.image_credit: Airman 1st Class Hannah Bench · DVIDS 9969464 · Public domain · Staff Sgts. Joshua Owens and Chaz Dages on an F-35A engine-run simulator, Misawa Air Base, Japan, Sept. 24, 2026.

political.hed: British police arrested five men near a U.S. bomber base in England
political.insight: Defense News, Sunday, citing Reuters: British police arrested five men near RAF Fairford after a tip that three vans were heading toward the airfield, which hosts U.S. Air Force personnel and has been used to strike Iran. President Trump said the suspects had been looking to do big damage and had been under investigation by British and U.S. authorities. Counter Terrorism Policing said the five remain in custody on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, and that police believe the incident is contained. A source familiar with the investigation told Reuters an Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely. Arrest report, not a completed prosecution.

political.hed: A report calls the Balkans an energy partner for Europe
political.insight: Heritage, posted overnight: the report says American energy security in Europe is moving fast enough that 2026 may later look like the turn toward a transatlantic energy arrangement, and it names the Balkans as a partner in that shift. Report, not a new treaty. The full text sits behind the site's reader wall; the headline and date are from the authorized feed.

political.hed: Treating a child as the opposite sex is not the legal definition of abuse, a report argues
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: institutions built to protect children are under scrutiny after parents lost custody for refusing to treat a gender-confused child as the opposite sex. The report says those cases rest on an ideological premise, not the legal definition of abuse. Report, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: The Navy is weighing foreign designs for the next small warship
tech.insight: USNI News, Sunday: both U.S. and foreign designs for the next small-surface combatant are under consideration after the cancellation of the Constellation-class guided-missile frigate, the new head of the Navy's shipbuilding enterprise said this week. A foreign design study is running in parallel with HII's FF(X) patrol frigate work. Design study, not a contract award.

culture.hed: A review says Thomas is on track to set the Court's longevity record
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: Mark Pulliam reviews Sen. Ted Cruz's Going Further, a book drawn from interviews with Justice Clarence Thomas. The review says Thomas, with 34 years on the Court, is in second place behind William O. Douglas and would pass Douglas's record on May 19, 2028, if he stays. Book review, not a retirement announcement.

culture.hed: WORLD reports on China's religious crackdowns
culture.insight: WORLD News Group, Thursday: the piece is filed under the headline Exposing China's religious crackdowns. WORLD's full text sits behind the site's reader wall; the headline and date are from the authorized feed. Report on persecution, not a new U.S. statute.
